member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Appointments.AppointmentManager
member.summary: Interacts with the user's Appointments provider from app data. Call static methods to display provider-specific UI so that the user can perform tasks.

member.name: M:Windows.ApplicationModel.Appointments.AppointmentManager.ShowAddAppointmentAsync(Windows.ApplicationModel.Appointments.Appointment,Windows.Foundation.Rect,Windows.UI.Popups.Placement)
member.summary: Shows the Appointments provider Add Appointment UI, to enable the user to add an appointment.
member.returns: When this method completes, it returns a String object that represents the appointment. This serves as an appointment identifier for future reference when updating or removing. If the appointment identifier returned is an empty string, the appointment was not added to the Appointments provider app.
member.param: The object representing the information for the appointment to add.

The Rect is the rectangular area of user selection (for example, pressing a button), around which the operating system displays the Add Appointment UI, not within that rectangular area. For example, if an app uses a button to show the Rect, pass the Rect of the button so the Add Appointment UI displays around the button, not overlapping it.
The Placement that describes the preferred placement of the Add Appointment UI.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.AlarmAccessStatus
member.summary: Indicates whether the user has given permission for the app to set alarms.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.AlarmAccessStatus.Unspecified
member.summary: The user has not responded to a permission request for the app to set alarms.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.AlarmAccessStatus.AllowedWithWakeupCapability
member.summary: The user has given permission for the app to set alarms, and alarms can wake up the computer from standby.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.AlarmAccessStatus.AllowedWithoutWakeupCapability
member.summary: The user has given permission for the app to set alarms, but the alarms cannot wake up the computer from standby.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.AlarmAccessStatus.Denied
member.summary: The user has denied permission for the app to set alarms.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundAccessStatus
member.summary: Specifies an app's ability to perform background activity and display a tile on the lock screen.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundAccessStatus.Unspecified
member.summary: The user has not selected "allow" or "don't allow" in the dialog box, or dismissed it without making a choice. The app cannot perform background activity in this state. However, it can request permission from the user to do so through the RequestAccessAsync method.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundAccessStatus.AllowedWithAlwaysOnRealTimeConnectivity
member.summary: The user chose "allow" in the dialog box. The app is added to the lock screen, can set up background tasks, and, if it has the capability, can use the real-time connectivity (RTC) broker. This means that the app can function while the device is in the connected standby state. After this value has been returned, subsequent calls to the RequestAccessAsync method do not present the dialog box to the user.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundAccessStatus.AllowedMayUseActiveRealTimeConnectivity
member.summary: The user chose "allow" in the dialog box. The app is added to the lock screen and can set up background tasks, but it cannot use the real-time connectivity (RTC) broker. This means that the app might not function while the device is in connected standby. Note that apps that do not specify RTC in their manifest will always demonstrate this behavior. After this value has been returned, subsequent calls to the RequestAccessAsync method do not present the dialog box to the user.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundAccessStatus.Denied
member.summary: The user chose "don't allow" in the dialog box. The app is not added to the lock screen. After this value has been returned, subsequent calls to the RequestAccessAsync method do not present the dialog box to the user.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundWorkCostValue.Medium
member.summary: Background resources are in use, but the background task can do some work.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundWorkCostValue.High

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason
member.summary: Specifies the reasons for cancelling a background task.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.Abort
member.summary: The background task was canceled by the application. This can happen for one of the following four reasons: The task is considered an idle task. This means that the background task is still running, but without doing anything - for example, a JavaScript task that does not call the close() function.The background task uses the MaintenanceTrigger and the system transitions to DC (battery power).The app unregisters the background task, in which case the task is cancelled if it is currently running.The app that registered the background task is uninstalled while the task is running.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.Terminating
member.summary: The background task was canceled because the application is about to be terminated due to system policy. The application should save any state that will be needed when the application restarts.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.LoggingOff
member.summary: The background task was canceled because the user has logged off the system.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.ServicingUpdate
member.summary: The background task was canceled because the application was updated.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.IdleTask
member.summary: The background task was canceled because it was active, but not doing any work.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.Uninstall
member.summary: The background task was canceled because the application was uninstalled.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.ConditionLoss
member.summary: The background task was canceled because one or more of its required conditions is no longer met.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.SystemPolicy
member.summary: The background task was cancelled because of system policy.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskCancellationReason.QuietHoursEntered
member.summary: The background task was cancelled because the device entered the quiet hours period.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.DeviceTriggerResult
member.summary: Indicates whether the device background task operation was allowed or denied, and if it was denied specifies the reason.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.DeviceTriggerResult.Allowed
member.summary: The device background task was triggered.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.DeviceTriggerResult.DeniedByUser
member.summary: The device background task was denied by the user.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.DeviceTriggerResult.DeniedBySystem
member.summary: The device background task was denied due to system policy.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.DeviceTriggerResult.LowBattery
member.summary: The device background task cannot run because the battery is low.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.LocationTriggerType
member.summary: Indicates a type of location event for a location background task trigger.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.LocationTriggerType.Geofence
member.summary: Indicates a geofence location trigger.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType
member.summary: Specifies a system condition that must be in effect for a background task to run. If a background task with a system condition is triggered, the task will not run until the condition is met.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.Invalid
member.summary: Not a valid condition type.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.UserPresent
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when the user is present. If a background task with the UserPresent condition is triggered, and the user is away, the task will not run until the user is present.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.UserNotPresent
member.summary: Specifies that background task can only run when the user is not present. If a background task with the UserNotPresent condition is triggered, and the user is present, the task will not run until the user becomes inactive.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.InternetAvailable
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when the Internet is available. If a background task with the InternetAvailable condition is triggered, and the Internet is not available, the task will not run until the Internet is available again.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.InternetNotAvailable
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when the Internet is not available. If a background task with the InternetNotAvailable condition is triggered, and the Internet is available, the task will not run until the Internet is unavailable.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.SessionConnected
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when the user's session is connected. If a background task with the SessionConnected condition is triggered, and the user session is not logged in, the task will run when the user logs in.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.SessionDisconnected
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when the user's session is disconnected. If a background task with the SessionDisconnected condition is triggered, and the user is logged in, the task will run when the user logs out.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.FreeNetworkAvailable
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when a free (non-metered) network connection is available.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemConditionType.BackgroundWorkCostNotHigh
member.summary: Specifies that the background task can only run when the cost to do background work is low.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemTriggerType
member.summary: Specifies the system events that can be used to trigger a background task.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemTriggerType.Invalid
member.summary: Not a valid trigger type.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemTriggerType.SmsReceived
member.summary: The background task is triggered when a new SMS message is received by an installed mobile broadband device.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemTriggerType.UserPresent
member.summary: The background task is triggered when the user becomes present.An app must be placed on the lock screen before it can successfully register background tasks using this trigger type.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemTriggerType.UserAway
member.summary: The background task is triggered when the user becomes absent.An app must be placed on the lock screen before it can successfully register background tasks using this trigger type.

member.name: F:Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.SystemTriggerType.NetworkStateChange
member.summary: The background task is triggered when a network change occurs, such as a change in cost or connectivity.

member.name: T:Windows.ApplicationModel.Contacts.ContactManager
member.summary: Represents a service that source apps can call to access contact data.

member.name: M:Windows.ApplicationModel.Contacts.ContactManager.ShowContactCard(Windows.ApplicationModel.Contacts.Contact,Windows.Foundation.Rect)
member.summary: Queries the operating system for a user's contact and shows the contact data in a contact card
member.param: The object that represents the contact that the app wants to display the contact card for. contact must contain at least an Id, Emails, or a phone number from a Phones list to query the user's contact database to retrieve a matching contact to display. Id has higher priority for querying. If an Id matches, the rest of query parameters will be ignored for matching purposes. If an Id does not find a match, the query uses the rest of query parameters. Emails and Phones have equal priority for matching. If multiple email addresses, or phone numbers, or both are provided, the query first performs an exact match, requiring all query parameters to match a system contact record. If this results in no matches, the query uses "best effort" match, in which a match of any query parameters is sufficient.In no matches occur, the data in the input contact displays in the contact card. If a match occurs, only system contact data displays, and the data in the input contact is discarded.

The Rect is the rectangular area of user selection (for example, pressing a button), around which the operating system displays the contact card, not within that rectangular area. For example, if an app uses a button to show the contact card, pass the Rect of the button so the contact card displays around the button, not overlapping it.

member.summary: Provides types and members for interacting with the Windows Store. You can use the members of this class to check the license state of the app and determine if it's a trial version or an active license. You can also check in-app features and enable in-app purchases. This class also allows you to simulate these functions before you submit the app to the Windows Store.

member.name: M:Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.DtdEntity.InsertBefore(Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode,Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode)
member.summary: Inserts a child node to the left of the specified node, or at the end of the child node list.
member.returns: On success, the child node that was inserted. If null, no object is created.
member.param: The address of the new node to be inserted. The node passed here must be a valid child of the current XML DOM document node. For example, if the current node is an attribute, you cannot pass another attribute in the newChild parameter, because an attribute cannot have an attribute as a child. If newChild is a DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT node type, all its children are inserted in order before referenceChild. If newChild is already in the tree, it is first removed before it is reinserted before the referenceChild node. Read-only nodes, such as NODE_DOCUMENT_TYPE and NODE_ENTITY nodes, cannot be passed in the newChild parameter.

The reference node. The node specified is where the newChild node is to be inserted to the left as the preceding sibling in the child list. The node passed here must be a either a child node of the current node or null. If the value is null, the newChild node is inserted at the end of the child list. If the referenceChild node is not a child of the current node, an error is returned.

member.name: M:Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.XmlAttribute.InsertBefore(Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode,Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode)
member.summary: Inserts a child node to the left of the specified node, or at the end of the child node list.
member.returns: On success, the child node that was inserted. If null, no object is created.
member.param: The address of the new node to be inserted. The node passed here must be a valid child of the current XML DOM document node. For example, if the current node is an attribute, you cannot pass another attribute in the newChild parameter, because an attribute cannot have an attribute as a child. If newChild is a DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT node type, all its children are inserted in order before referenceChild. If newChild is already in the tree, it is first removed before it is reinserted before the referenceChild node. Read-only nodes, such as NODE_DOCUMENT_TYPE and NODE_ENTITY nodes, cannot be passed in the newChild parameter.

The reference node. The node specified is where the newChild node is to be inserted to the left as the preceding sibling in the child list. The node passed here must be a either a child node of the current node or null. If the value is null, the newChild node is inserted at the end of the child list. If the referenceChild node is not a child of the current node, an error is returned.

If newChild is already in the tree, it is first removed before it is reinserted before the referenceChild node. Read-only nodes, such as NODE_DOCUMENT_TYPE and NODE_ENTITY nodes, cannot be passed in the newChild parameter.

The reference node. The node specified is where the newChild node is to be inserted to the left as the preceding sibling in the child list. The node passed here must be a either a child node of the current node or null. If the value is null, the newChild node is inserted at the end of the child list. If the referenceChild node is not a child of the current node, an error is returned.

member.name: M:Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.XmlDocumentType.InsertBefore(Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode,Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode)
member.summary: Inserts a child node to the left of the specified node, or at the end of the list.
member.returns: On success, the child node that was inserted. If null, no object is created.
member.param: The address of the new node to be inserted. The node passed here must be a valid child of the current XML DOM document node. For example, if the current node is an attribute, you cannot pass another attribute in the newChild parameter, because an attribute cannot have an attribute as a child. If newChild is a DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT node type, all its children are inserted in order before referenceChild. If newChild is already in the tree, it is first removed before it is reinserted before the referenceChild node. Read-only nodes, such as NODE_DOCUMENT_TYPE and NODE_ENTITY nodes, cannot be passed in the newChild parameter.

The reference node. The node specified is where the newChild node is to be inserted to the left as the preceding sibling in the child list. The node passed here must be a either a child node of the current node or null. If the value is null, the newChild node is inserted at the end of the child list. If the referenceChild node is not a child of the current node, an error is returned.

member.name: M:Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.XmlProcessingInstruction.InsertBefore(Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode,Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode)
member.summary: Inserts a child node to the left of the specified node, or at the end of the list.
member.returns: On success, the child node that was inserted. If null, no object is created.
member.param: The address of the new node to be inserted. The node passed here must be a valid child of the current XML DOM document node. For example, if the current node is an attribute, you cannot pass another attribute in the newChild parameter, because an attribute cannot have an attribute as a child. If newChild is a DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT node type, all its children are inserted in order before referenceChild. If newChild is already in the tree, it is first removed before it is reinserted before the referenceChild node. Read-only nodes, such as NODE_DOCUMENT_TYPE and NODE_ENTITY nodes, cannot be passed in the newChild parameter.

The reference node. The node specified is where the newChild node is to be inserted to the left as the preceding sibling in the child list. The node passed here must be a either a child node of the current node or null. If the value is null, the newChild node is inserted at the end of the child list. If the referenceChild node is not a child of the current node, an error is returned.

member.name: M:Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode.InsertBefore(Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode,Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.IXmlNode)
member.summary: Inserts a child node to the left of the specified node, or at the end of the list.
member.returns: On success, the child node that was inserted. If null, no object is created.
member.param: The address of the new node to be inserted. The node passed here must be a valid child of the current XML DOM document node. For example, if the current node is an attribute, you cannot pass another attribute in the newChild parameter, because an attribute cannot have an attribute as a child. If newChild is a DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT node type, all its children are inserted in order before referenceChild. If newChild is already in the tree, it is first removed before it is reinserted before the referenceChild node. Read-only nodes, such as NODE_DOCUMENT_TYPE and NODE_ENTITY nodes, cannot be passed in the newChild parameter.

The reference node. The node specified is where the newChild node is to be inserted to the left as the preceding sibling in the child list. The node passed here must be a either a child node of the current node or null. If the value is null, the newChild node is inserted at the end of the child list. If the referenceChild node is not a child of the current node, an error is returned.

member.name: N:Windows.Devices.Geolocation.Geofencing
member.summary: Windows 8.1 introduces support for geofencing. Geofencing allows an app to define a radius around a point of interest and have the system alert the app when entering or exiting that area.The geofencing capabilities supported by Windows 8.1 allow you to:Create one or more geofences, or areas of interest.Set a notification to occur when entering a geofence.Set a notification to occur when leaving a geofence.Remove a geofence.Allow your geofence app to run in the background and continue to get geofence events. Note that this is applicable to apps which are on the lock screen only.Test the geofencing features of your app by using a simulator to simulate movement in and out of the geofence. These features will enable apps to provide features such as reminders to a user who is leaving work or home or displaying coupons when the user is near certain stores. The Windows.Devices.Geolocation.Geofencing namespace contains the classes needed to do geofencing. The workflow generally consists of creating a one or more Geofence objects that define the areas of interest and the notification conditions. Then your app must handle the events that occur when entering or exiting one of the geofences. If your app is running in the background, you need to use the new background LocationTrigger creating a background task.

This id can be retrieved from Windows.Devices.Enumeration or the DeviceInformationId property of the AutoPlay device event arguments. For more information, see Quickstart: Register an app for an AutoPlay device. In order for FromId to succeed, the app must declare both the removableStorage capability as shown in the App capability declarations and file type associations for the files it wishes to access on the device as shown in How to handle file activation. For more information, see the Removable Storage sample.

member.summary: 24-bit RGB color (3 channels at 8 bits per channel).

member.summary: 8 bit or 4 bit grayscale (1 channel at 8 or 4 bits per channel). If the device supports both 4 and 8 bit grayscale the DefaultColorMode property will use 8 bit.

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerColorMode.Monochrome
member.summary: 1 bit bi-tonal, also called monochrome or 'black and white' (1 channel at 1 bit per channel).

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerColorMode.AutoColor
member.summary: The device automatically detects the right color mode based on the scan content. In this case the decision between color, grayscale and black and white for example relies on the device, and not the app.

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat
member.summary: The type of files to scan to.

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.Jpeg
member.summary: Exchangeable image file format/EXIF or JPEG file interchange format/JFIF Use these files only in color or grayscale modes (8 bits per channel/sample), with single page and compressed (lossy JPEG compression).

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.Png
member.summary: Portable Network Graphics (PNG) image file format This value supports any color mode, with single page and compressed (loseless PNG compression).

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.DeviceIndependentBitmap
member.summary: Windows Device Independent Bitmap (DIB) This value supports any color mode, with single page and uncompressed. This is the only format that is supported by all compatible WIA 2.0 scanner devices.

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.Tiff
member.summary: Uncompressed Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) compatible with the TIFF 6.0 specification, either single and/or multi-page These files can be in any color mode supported by this API, always uncompressed and either single page (if only one image has to be transferred) or multi-page (if multiple images have to be transferred and the device supports this multi-page file format).

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.Xps
member.summary: Microsoft XML Paper Specification (XPS) document file format These files can contain image data in any color mode supported by this API, compressed at the choice of the device, either single or multi-page.

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.OpenXps
member.summary: Open XML Paper Specification (OpenXPS) document file format These files can contain image data in any color mode supported by this API, compressed at the choice of the device, either single or multi-page.

member.name: F:Windows.Devices.Scanners.ImageScannerFormat.Pdf
member.summary: Portable Document Format PDF/A (PDF/A is an ISO-standardized version of the Portable Document Format/PDF specialized for the digital preservation of electronic documents) document file format These files can contain image data in any color mode supported by this API, compressed at the choice of the device, either single or multi-page.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.SmsReceivedEventDetails.DeviceId
member.summary: Returns the DeviceInformation ID of the network interface that received the SMS message. This ID can be passed to SmsDevice.FromIdAsync to activate the device and retrieve additional message details.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A string containing the DeviceInformation ID of the SMS network interface (device). This value is typically used to retrieve details such as the sender and the body of the message. For example, you might use the ID to display a popup telling the user that a new message from a particular person has arrived. The combination of DeviceId and MessageIndex is sufficient to retrieve the new message from the SMS device.

member.returns: An integer index of the new message.

member.summary: Decodes a binary message and places the results in a new instance of a text message. This method represents the binary message as a reference to a buffer of bytes and a selection of how the buffer is encoded. Therefore, it can be used when the message did not originate directly from the device or as an instance of an SmsBinaryMessage class.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A new SmsTextMessage object if the decoding was successful.
member.param: An SmsDataFormat enumerated value that identifies the format of a particular protocol description unit (PDU) buffer.
An array of bytes containing the binary data to decode.

member.summary: Indicates the part number of a multi-part message if this message is part of a multi-part message. It can be used to reconstruct the original message by joining the parts together, in conjunction with the PartReferenceId and PartCount properties.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An unsigned integer. It is one-based. It will not exceed PartCount + 1.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.SmsTextMessage.PartReferenceId
member.summary: Indicates a reference value that can be used if the message is part of a multi-part message. If this message belongs to a multi-part message, the PartNumber value can be used to reconstruct the full original message, and each part of that message will have the same value for PartReferenceId.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An unsigned integer determined by the sending network; it cannot be manipulated through this interface. If the network has its own policy on the lifetime of a multi-part message, this reference number might not be valid indefinitely.

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsBinaryMessage
member.summary: This interface provides access to the raw binary format of an SMS message. The message is stored in the industry standard protocol description unit (PDU) format (see the SMS specification GSM 03.40).

member.summary: Retrieves the detected protocol description unit (PDU) format of this message.

member.summary: Specifies the raw binary payload of the SMS message. It should be formatted according to the protocol description unit (PDU) standard.

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice
member.summary: This interface controls a mobile broadband SMS device. It is the primary entry point to SMS services on the device.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.AccountPhoneNumber
member.summary: Returns the phone number associated with the SMS device. The phone number can be used to associate incoming messages with the account and possibly an external storage mechanism such as an account inbox.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A string representation of the account phone number.

member.name: M:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.CalculateLength(Windows.Devices.Sms.SmsTextMessage)
member.summary: Estimates the transmitted message length of the specified text message. The estimate can be useful to clients who want to give an indication of how many messages will be sent on the network to carry the text of the full message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A reference to an SmsEncodedLength structure that is populated with the length information.
member.param: A reference to the SMS text message to measure.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.CellularClass
member.summary: Returns the cellular class of the SMS device. The class can be used to determine which encodings are appropriate or which device limitations are in effect.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An enumerated value indicating the device's cellular class.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.DeviceStatus
member.summary: Returns the SMS device's status, which indicates whether the device is ready, or not. It also indcates what type of problem exists if the device is not ready.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An enumerated value that indicates the readiness of an SMS device to engage in cellular network traffic operations.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.MessageStore

member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.

member.name: M:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.SendMessageAsync(Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsMessage)

member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.

member.param: A reference to an SmsMessage object. The message can be in text or binary format.

member.name: E:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsDevice.SmsMessageReceived

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsMessage

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsMessage.MessageClass
member.summary: Returns the message class, as determined by the operator's message network. The two most common classes are None (normal message) or Class0 (special operator message, such as a roaming warning that must be shown immediately to the user). A typical client for end-user messages ignores Class0 messages.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A value from the SmsMessageClass enumeration.

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage
member.summary: This interface manipulates a decoded SMS text message. It provides direct access to the plain text body of the message, as well as key header properties, such as time stamp.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.Body
member.summary: Specifies the plain text body of the message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A string representing the body of the text message. If there were decoding problems, some characters in the original message can be represented by a wildcard character, typically a question mark: '?'.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.Encoding
member.summary: Specifies the encoding type that has been set to use when sending this message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A value from the SmsEncoding enumeration.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.From
member.summary: Specifies the phone number of the sender of the message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A string representation of the phone number of the sender of this message. It should be in the format preferred by the device and the network it is registered on.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.PartCount
member.summary: Retrieves the total number of parts in the original message if the message is part of a multi-part message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An unsigned integer. If the message is standalone, the value is 1.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.PartNumber
member.summary: Retrieves the part number of a multi-part message if this message is part of a multi-part message. It can be used to reconstruct the original message by joining the parts together, in conjunction with the PartReferenceId and PartCount properties.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An unsigned integer. It is one-based. It will not exceed PartCount + 1.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.PartReferenceId
member.summary: Indicates a reference value that can be used if the message is part of a multi-part message. If this message belongs to a multi-part message, the PartNumber value can be used to reconstruct the full original message, and each part of that message will have the same value for PartReferenceId.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: An unsigned integer determined by the sending network; it cannot be manipulated through this interface. If the network has its own policy on the lifetime of a multi-part message, this reference number might not be valid indefinitely.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.Timestamp
member.summary: Retrieves the timestamp of the message. It is determined locally for a constructed message instance or from the service center timestamp of a received message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A value of the DateTime type.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.To
member.summary: Specifies the recipient phone number of this message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: A string representation of the phone number, formatted in the phone number format favored by the device and the network that the device is registered on.

member.name: M:Windows.Devices.Sms.ISmsTextMessage.ToBinaryMessages(Windows.Devices.Sms.SmsDataFormat)
member.summary: Reads a message in the specified format and places the results in a new instance of a binary message.
member.capability: Required to access the SMS service.
member.returns: The new binary message that holds the result of this method call.
member.param: A value from the SmsDataFormat enumeration.

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Sms.SmsMessageReceivedEventHandler

member.name: N:Windows.Devices.Usb
member.summary: The Windows.Devices.Usb defines Windows Runtime classes that a Windows store app can use to communicate with a USB device that does not belong to a device class, or for which Microsoft does not provide an in-box driver.

member.name: T:Windows.Devices.Usb.UsbBulkInEndpointDescriptor
member.summary: The endpoint descriptor for a USB bulk IN endpoint. The descriptor specifies the endpoint type, direction, number and also the maximum number of bytes that can be read from the endpoint, in a single transfer.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Usb.UsbBulkInEndpointDescriptor.EndpointNumber
member.summary: Gets the USB endpoint number of the bulk IN endpoint.
member.returns: The endpoint number of the bulk IN endpoint. That number is in Bit 3...0 of the bEndpointAddress field of an endpoint descriptor. For information, see Table 9-13 in the Universal Serial Bus Specification (version 2.0) or Table 9-18 in the Universal Serial Bus 3.0 Specification.

member.name: P:Windows.Devices.Usb.UsbBulkInEndpointDescriptor.MaxPacketSize
member.summary: Gets the maximum number of bytes that can be sent to or received from this endpoint, in a single packet.
member.returns: Indicates the maximum packet size of the endpoint. This value is derived from the wMaxPacketSize field value of the endpoint descriptor. For information, see Table 9-13 in the Universal Serial Bus Specification (version 2.0) or Table 9-18 in the Universal Serial Bus 3.0 Specification.

member.returns: One of the following values:Return valueDescriptionLess than zeroThe date and time of this calendar is earlier than that of other.ZeroThe date and times are equal.Greater than zeroThe date and time of this calendar is later than that of other.
member.param: The DateTime object to compare to the current calendar.

member.summary: Returns the abbreviated time zone name applicable at the instant of time that this Calendar object represents.

member.name: T:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion
member.summary: Describes a region. This is usually a country, but may be a macroregion.

member.name: M:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.#ctor
member.summary: Creates a GeographicRegion object that defaults to the user's home region.

member.name: M:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Creates a GeographicRegion object.
member.param: One of the ISO 3166-1 two-letter or three-letter codes that identify the country, or one of the three-digit UN-M49 codes that identify the geographical region.

member.name: M:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.IsSupported(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether a geographic region identifier is supported.
member.returns: True if the ID is known; otherwise, false. If this method returns true, an app can safely construct a region by using this region identifier. If it returns false, attempting to construct a region for the given code will throw an exception.
member.param: One of the ISO 3166-1 two-letter or three-letter codes that identify the country, or one of the three-digit UN-M49 codes that identify the geographical region.

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.CurrenciesInUse
member.summary: Gets the set of currencies in use in this region.
member.returns: The set of ISO 4217 3-letter codes for the currencies that are used in the region.

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.Code
member.summary: Gets the string that contains the best available identifier that represents the region.
member.returns: Returns a string that contains: The two-letter identifier code, if one exists (and is not "ZZ"); otherwise, the three-letter identifier code, if one exists (and is not "ZZZ"); otherwise, the three-digit numeric identifier code, if one exists (and is not "999"); otherwise, "ZZ".

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.CodeThreeDigit
member.summary: Gets the three-digit identifier for this region, as a string.
member.returns: Returns as a string the ISO-3166-1 numeric three-digit code for the region, or the UN-M49 code. If the region is unknown, returns "999".

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.CodeThreeLetter
member.summary: Gets the three-letter identifier for this region.
member.returns: Returns the three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code for this region, if one exists; otherwise, returns "ZZZ".

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.CodeTwoLetter
member.summary: Gets the two-letter identifier for this region.
member.returns: Returns the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for this region, if one exists; otherwise, returns "ZZ".

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.DisplayName
member.summary: Gets a localized string that is suitable for display to the user for identifying the region.
member.returns: The localized name of the region.

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.GeographicRegion.NativeName
member.summary: Gets the name of the region in the primary language spoken in this region.
member.returns: The name of the region in the primary language spoken in this region.

member.name: T:Windows.Globalization.Language
member.summary: A class that provides information related to BCP-47 language tags such as the language name and the script.

member.name: M:Windows.Globalization.Language.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Creates a Language object.
member.param: A BCP-47 language tag. See Remarks.

member.name: M:Windows.Globalization.Language.GetExtensionSubtags(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves a vector of extension subtags in the current language for the given extension identified by singleton.
member.returns: The list of extension subtags identified by singleton.
member.param: A single-character subtag for the LanguageTag of the current language. See BCP-47 language tags, Extensions and the Extensions Registry.

member.name: M:Windows.Globalization.Language.IsWellFormed(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether a BCP-47 language tag is well-formed.
member.returns: True if the language tag is well-formed as defined by BCP-47, except when the language tag can never be valid according to BCP-47. Otherwise it returns false. If this method returns true, an application can safely construct a language by using this tag. If it returns false, attempting to construct a language for the given tag will throw an exception.
member.param: A BCP-47 language tag.

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.Language.CurrentInputMethodLanguageTag
member.summary: Gets the BCP-47 language tag for the currently enabled keyboard layout or Input Method Editor (IME).
member.returns: The BCP-47 language tag.

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.Language.DisplayName
member.summary: Gets a localized string that is suitable for display to the user for identifying the language.
member.returns: The localized name of the language.

member.name: P:Windows.Globalization.Language.LanguageTag
member.summary: Gets the normalized BCP-47 language tag for this language.

member.name: T:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm
member.summary: Specifies the algorithm used to round numbers.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.None
member.summary: No rounding is performed.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundDown
member.summary: Round towards negative infinity. (Return the largest integer, increment, or significant digit which does not exceed the input.)

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundUp
member.summary: Round towards infinity. (Return the smallest integer, increment, or significant digit which is not less than the input.)

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundTowardsZero
member.summary: Round towards zero. This is the equivalent of RoundDown if the input is positive, or RoundUp if the input is negative.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundAwayFromZero
member.summary: Round away from zero. This is the equivalent of RoundUp if the input is positive, or RoundDown if the input is negative.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundHalfDown
member.summary: Round to the integer, increment, or significant digit that is closest to the input. If the input is exactly halfway between the possible outputs, this is the equivalent of RoundDown.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundHalfUp
member.summary: Round to the integer, increment, or significant digit that is closest to the input. If the input is exactly halfway between the possible outputs, this is the equivalent of RoundUp.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundHalfTowardsZero
member.summary: Round to the integer, increment, or significant digit that is closest to the input. If the input is exactly halfway between the possible outputs, this is the equivalent of RoundTowardsZero.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundHalfAwayFromZero
member.summary: Round to the integer, increment, or significant digit that is closest to the input. If the input is exactly halfway between the possible outputs, this is the equivalent of RoundAwayFromZero.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundHalfToEven
member.summary: Round to the integer, increment, or significant digit that is closest to the input. If the input is exactly halfway between the possible outputs, round to the nearest even output.

member.name: F:Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.RoundingAlgorithm.RoundHalfToOdd
member.summary: Round to the integer, increment, or significant digit that is closest to the input. If the input is exactly halfway between the possible outputs, round to the nearest odd output.

member.summary: Specifies that the monitor is oriented in landscape mode where the width of the display viewing area is greater than the height.

member.name: F:Windows.Graphics.Display.DisplayOrientations.Portrait
member.summary: Specifies that the monitor rotated 90 degrees in the clockwise direction to orient the display in portrait mode where the height of the display viewing area is greater than the width.

member.name: F:Windows.Graphics.Display.DisplayOrientations.LandscapeFlipped
member.summary: Specifies that the monitor rotated another 90 degrees in the clockwise direction (to equal 180 degrees) to orient the display in landscape mode where the width of the display viewing area is greater than the height. This landscape mode is flipped 180 degrees from the Landscape mode.

member.name: F:Windows.Graphics.Display.DisplayOrientations.PortraitFlipped
member.summary: Specifies that the monitor rotated another 90 degrees in the clockwise direction (to equal 270 degrees) to orient the display in portrait mode where the height of the display viewing area is greater than the width. This portrait mode is flipped 180 degrees from the Portrait mode.

member.name: F:Windows.Management.Deployment.DeploymentOptions.InstallAllResources
member.summary: When you set this option, the app is instructed to skip resource applicability checks. This effectively stages or registers all resource packages that a user passes in to the command, which forces applicability for all packages contained in a bundle. If a user passes in a bundle, all contained resource packages will be registered.

member.summary: Local network access only.

member.name: F:Windows.Networking.Connectivity.NetworkConnectivityLevel.ConstrainedInternetAccess
member.summary: Limited internet access. This value indicates captive portal connectivity, where local access to a web portal is provided, but access to the Internet requires that specific credentials are provided via the portal. This level of connectivity is generally encountered when using connections hosted in public locations (e.g. coffee shops and book stores). This doesn't guarantee detection of a captive portal. Windows Store apps should also test if the captive portal can be reached using a URL for the captive portal, or by attempting access to a public web site which will then redirect to the captive portal when Windows reports LocalAccess as the current NetworkConnectivityLevel.

member.summary: Specifies an IEEE 802.11i RSNA algorithm that uses PSK. IEEE 802.1X port authorization is performed by the supplicant and authenticator. Cipher keys are dynamically derived through a pre-shared key that is used on both the supplicant and authenticator.

member.name: M:Windows.Networking.NetworkOperators.HotspotAuthenticationContext.IssueCredentials(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Provides credentials to Windows for hotspot authentication
member.param: The UserName parameter of the Wireless Internet Service Provider roaming (WISPr) authentication protocol. IssueCredentials performs URL encoding before submitting the value to the server. If this string is empty, the corresponding authentication parameter is skipped.

The Password parameter of the WISPr authentication protocol. IssueCredentials performs URL encoding before submitting the value to the server. If this string is empty, the corresponding authentication parameter is skipped.

Additional parameters to be appended to the authentication string. IssueCredentials appends this parameter after an & character to the HTTP POST string as is without any encoding. This can be used to add multiple parameters. The default for this parameter is an empty string.

If true, an application permanently disables the auto-connect property on a connection. If authentication fails, the connection will be disconnected and not retried in the current user session. Otherwise, false.

member.name: M:Windows.Networking.NetworkOperators.HotspotAuthenticationContext.IssueCredentialsAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Asynchronously provides credentials to Windows for hotspot authentication

member.param: The UserName parameter of the Wireless Internet Service Provider roaming (WISPr) authentication protocol. IssueCredentials performs URL encoding before submitting the value to the server. If this string is empty, the corresponding authentication parameter is skipped.

The Password parameter of the WISPr authentication protocol. IssueCredentials performs URL encoding before submitting the value to the server. If this string is empty, the corresponding authentication parameter is skipped.

Additional parameters to be appended to the authentication string. IssueCredentials appends this parameter after an & character to the HTTP POST string as is without any encoding. This can be used to add multiple parameters. The default for this parameter is an empty string.

If true, an application permanently disables the auto-connect property on a connection. If authentication fails, the connection will be disconnected and not retried in the current user session. Otherwise, false.

This member can change from true to false if the app sends less data.

member.name: F:Windows.Networking.Sockets.ControlChannelTriggerStatus.TransportDisconnected
member.summary: The network transport associated with the ControlChannelTrigger was disconnected. The underlying TCP connection was already disconnected by a TCP reset received from the remote destination or a graceful disconnect by either the app or the remote destination. The most common occurrence is a TCP reset or a graceful disconnect sent by the remote destination.

member.name: F:Windows.Networking.Sockets.ControlChannelTriggerStatus.ServiceUnavailable
member.summary: The service provided by the ControlChannelTrigger is unavailable. This can happen if the network connection broker service is not yet ready but the app is trying to establish a ControlChannelTrigger channel. This status code is provided under the following conditions:When there is fast user switching and the new user is trying to establish the ControlChannelTrigger channel.When the system is entering a low power mode (Connected standby mode) and the app is trying to create a software slot. Software slots are available only when the system is active and not in low power mode. The mitigation in both these cases is to listen for System Event broker events and register the ControlChannelTrigger channel at that point.

member.name: M:Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicEngine.Encrypt(Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicKey,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer)
member.summary: Encrypts data by using a symmetric or asymmetric algorithm.
member.returns: Encrypted data.
member.param: Cryptographic key to use for encryption. This can be an asymmetric or a symmetric key. For more information, see AsymmetricKeyAlgorithmProvider and SymmetricKeyAlgorithmProvider.
Data to encrypt.

Buffer that contains the initialization vector. This can be null for a symmetric algorithm and should always be null for an asymmetric algorithm. If an initialization vector (IV) was used to encrypt the data, you must use the same IV to decrypt the data. You can use the GenerateRandom method to create an IV that contains random data. Other IVs, such as nonce-generated vectors, require custom implementation. For more information, see Symmetric Key Encryption.Cipher block chaining (CBC) block cipher mode algorithms require an initialization vector. For more information, see Remarks.

member.name: M:Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicEngine.EncryptAndAuthenticate(Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicKey,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer)
member.summary: Performs authenticated encryption.
member.returns: The encrypted and authenticated data.If the method fails, authentication fails; if the method succeeds, the authentication succeeded as well.
member.param: Symmetric key to use for encryption.
Data to be encrypted and authenticated.

Nonce to be used. A nonce is a variable that has minimal chance of repeating. For example, you can use a random value that is newly generated for each use, a time stamp, a sequence number, or some combination of these. The Microsoft GCM implementation requires a 12-byte nonce. The CCM implementation requires a 7- to 13- byte nonce.
Authenticated data. This can be Null.

member.summary: The file stream is accessed in read-only mode. If the file is changed, subsequent read operations will fail. Multiple, independent read-only streams may be used to read a file. We recommend you keep read-only file streams open only while your app is actively reading from the file. You can close a stream by calling Close.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.FileAccessMode.ReadWrite

member.summary: Replace the existing file or folder. Your app must have permission to access the location that contains the existing file or folder. Access to a location can be granted in several ways, for example, by a capability declared in your application's manifest, or by the user through the file picker. You can use Windows.Storage.AccessCache to manage the list of locations that are accessible to your app via the file picker.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.StorageDeleteOption.PermanentDelete

member.name: M:Windows.Storage.BulkAccess.FileInformationFactory.#ctor(Windows.Storage.Search.IStorageQueryResultBase,Windows.Storage.FileProperties.ThumbnailMode,System.UInt32,Windows.Storage.FileProperties.ThumbnailOptions)
member.summary: Creates a new FileInformationFactory object that retrieves information about the StorageFile and StorageFolder objects in the specified query result, and that specifies the requested size and options for thumbnails that are retrieved for the objects.
member.param: The result of a query of files and folders on the system.To learn about query result objects, see StorageFileQueryResult, StorageFolderQueryResult, and StorageItemQueryResult.
A value that indicates the type of thumbnail view to retrieve for the StorageFile and StorageFolder.
The requested minimum size, in pixels, of the StorageFile and StorageFolder thumbnails.If thumbnails are not required for IStorageItemInformation objects, set the requestedSize to 0.

The thumbnail retrieval options.If you're using FileInformationFactory with the JavaScript ListView or XAML ListView and GridView controls, don't specify ThumbnailOptions.ReturnOnlyIfCached because this mode may prevent the control from being correctly populated with thumbnails.

member.name: M:Windows.Storage.BulkAccess.FileInformationFactory.#ctor(Windows.Storage.Search.IStorageQueryResultBase,Windows.Storage.FileProperties.ThumbnailMode,System.UInt32,Windows.Storage.FileProperties.ThumbnailOptions,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a new FileInformationFactory object that retrieves information about the StorageFile and StorageFolder objects in the specified query result, specifies the requested size and options for thumbnails that are retrieved for the objects, and indicates whether to delay loading information.
member.param: The result of a query of files and folders on the system.To learn about query result objects, see StorageFileQueryResult, StorageFolderQueryResult, and StorageItemQueryResult.
A value that indicates the type of thumbnail view to retrieve for the StorageFile and StorageFolder.
The requested minimum size, in pixels, of the StorageFile and StorageFolder thumbnails.If thumbnails are not required for IStorageItemInformation objects, set the requestedSize to 0.

The thumbnail retrieval options.If you're using FileInformationFactory with the JavaScript ListView or XAML ListView and GridView controls, don't specify ThumbnailOptions.ReturnOnlyIfCached because this mode may prevent the control from being correctly populated with thumbnails.

True to delay loading information; otherwise false. By default, this option is false and delay loading is not used.If delayLoad is true, it authorizes the FileInformationFactory to return IStorageItemInformation objects before thumbnails are available. Subsequently, the system fires a ThumbnailUpdated event when thumbnails become available. Using delay loading is recommended because it makes apps seem more responsive.If delayLoad is false (as it is by default), the system will require more time to retrieve IStorageItemInformation objects, but after the objects are retrieved all cached thumbnails will be accessible synchronously. Thumbnails that are not cached must still be accessed asynchronously in response to the ThumbnailUpdated event.

member.summary: Configures update policies for a local file.
member.param: The local file.

A unique identifier for the local file. You can use this identifier to associate a file in your app's repository with the local file. When updates are requested by Windows, you can use this contentId to identify the correct file in your app's repository.
A value that specifies whether Windows will request updates before the local file is read by other apps.
A value that specifies whether other apps can write to the local file and, if so, whether Windows will request updates after the local file is written.

For example, you could require Windows to request an update every time the local file is accessed by using CachedFileOptions.RequireUpdateOnAccess. For more information about possible options, see CachedFileOptions.

If the app that provides updates requests UI by completing its response to a FileUpdateRequested event and setting the FileUpdateRequest.Status to FileUpdateStatus.UserInputNeeded, the app will be closed immediately and the failure may be reported to the app that triggered the updates.

member.name: M:Windows.Storage.Search.QueryOptions.SetThumbnailPrefetch(Windows.Storage.FileProperties.ThumbnailMode,System.UInt32,Windows.Storage.FileProperties.ThumbnailOptions)
member.summary: Specifies the type and size of thumbnails that the system should start loading immediately when items are accessed (instead of retrieving them on a case-by-case basis).
member.param: The enumeration value that describes the purpose of the thumbnail and determines how the thumbnail image is adjusted. For guidance about choosing the best thumbnail mode, see Guidelines and checklist for thumbnails.

The requested size, in pixels, of the longest edge of the thumbnail. Windows uses the requestedSize as a guide and tries to return a thumbnail image that can be scaled to the requested size without reducing the quality of the image. If Windows can't find a thumbnail image that exactly meets the requested size, a larger thumbnail might be returned. If no larger thumbnail is available, a thumbnail image that is smaller than the requested size might be returned.

The enum value that describes the desired behavior to use to retrieve the thumbnail image. The specified behavior might affect the size and/or quality of the image and how quickly the thumbnail image is retrieved.

member.param: A value that specifies the set of properties to retrieve in advance. The possible property sets match the sets of properties available on from the StorageFile class. For example, PropertyPrefetchOptions.BasicProperties will retrieve all of the properties available through StorageFile.GetBasicPropertiesAsync in advance.

A custom list of properties to retrieve in advance as an array of property names. Use the system property names to specify properties, for example System.Copyright and System.Image.ColorSpace. A list of additional properties to retrieve.

member.param: An enumeration value that specifies the search parameters to use to query files. The CommonFileQuery enumeration provides search parameters for several common types of file queries. For example, deep queries that retrieve all the files in the folder where the query is created or shallow queries that retrieve only the files in the top-level of the folder. The enumeration also determines how query results are sorted.
An array of file types to be included in the query results. To include all file types, supply null or an array containing a single entry of *.

member.name: M:Windows.Storage.Search.QueryOptions.#ctor(Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery)
member.summary: Creates an instance of the QueryOptions class for enumerating subfolders and initializes it with values based on the specified CommonFolderQuery.
member.param: An enumeration value that specifies how to group the contents of the folder where the query is created into subfolders to enumerate. The subfolders that are retrieved using a CommonFolderQuery can be actual file system folders or virtual folders that represent groups of files (which are determined by the CommonFolderQuery value). For example, the CommonFolderQuery.GroupByArtist uses the Artist of the files in the folder (and its subfolders) to group files, creating one virtual folder (or file group) for each artist.

member.name: T:Windows.System.Threading.Core.PreallocatedWorkItem
member.summary: A preallocated work item is constructed in advance of its submission to the thread pool, ensuring that the work item is constructed so that it can be submitted to the thread pool when necessary. member.name: T:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority
member.summary: Defines the priority for window event dispatches.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Idle
member.summary: Lowest priority. Use this priority for background tasks. Delegates are processed when the window's main thread is idle and there is no input pending in the queue.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Low
member.summary: Low priority. Delegates are processed if there are no higher priority events pending in the queue.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Normal
member.summary: Normal priority. Delegates are processed in the order they are scheduled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.High
member.summary: High priority. Delegates are invoked immediately for all synchronous requests. Asynchronous requests are queued and processed before any other request type.Do not use this priority level in your app. It is reserved for system events. Using this priority can lead to the starvation of other messages, including system events.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Core.CoreProcessEventsOption
member.summary: Specifies the set of exclusive event-processing options passed to ProcessEvents.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreProcessEventsOption.ProcessOneAndAllPending
member.summary: Dispatch all currently available events in the queue. If no events are pending, wait for the next new event.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreProcessEventsOption.ProcessOneIfPresent
member.summary: Dispatch one event if it is currently pending in the queue. If no events are pending, do not wait for a new event to be raised but instead return immediately.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreProcessEventsOption.ProcessUntilQuit
member.summary: Wait for new events and dispatch all available events. Continue this behavior until the window is closed or the application calls the Close method on the CoreWindow instance.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreProcessEventsOption.ProcessAllIfPresent
member.summary: Dispatch all events currently pending in the queue. If no events are pending, do not wait for a new event to be raised but instead return immediately. This option is provided specifically for view provider implementations with IFrameworkView, and to be used in Windows Store app using DirectX with C++.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindowFlowDirection
member.summary: Specifies the flow order for text in a window.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindowFlowDirection.LeftToRight

member.returns: The extended usage of the raw input pointer.
member.param: The Human Interface Device (HID) usage page of the pointer device. Usage pages specify the class of device. For example, touch digitizers (0x0D) and generic input (0x01).

Indicates a usage in a usage page.Usage ID specify a device or property in the usagePage. For example, for touch digitizers this includes tip switch (0x42) to indicate finger contact or tip pressure (0x30).

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState
member.summary: Specifies the possible states of the CrossSliding event.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.Started
member.summary: A CrossSliding interaction has been detected.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.Dragging
member.summary: A CrossSliding interaction has started but the swipe or slide gesture has not crossed the minimum distance threshold for a selection action. (See the Remarks section for a diagram showing the CrossSliding distance thresholds.)There is no correlation between Dragging in CrossSlidingState (touch) and DraggingState (mouse or pen/stylus).

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.Selecting
member.summary: The swipe or slide gesture has crossed the minimum distance threshold for a selection action but has not crossed the minimum distance threshold of the rearrange action. This state is valid only when SpeedBumpStart is disabled in a GestureRecognizer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.SelectSpeedBumping
member.summary: The swipe or slide gesture has crossed the minimum distance threshold for a selection action (and the selection speed bump) but has not crossed the maximum distance threshold of the selection speed bump. This state is valid only when both SpeedBumpStart and SelectionStart are enabled in a GestureRecognizer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.SpeedBumping
member.summary: The swipe or slide gesture has crossed the minimum distance threshold for a selection action (and the selection speed bump) but has not crossed the maximum distance threshold of the selection speed bump. This state is valid only when SpeedBumpStart is enabled and SelectionStart is disabled in a GestureRecognizer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.Rearranging
member.summary: The swipe or slide gesture has crossed the minimum distance threshold of the rearrange action. This state is valid only when RearrangeStart is enabled in a GestureRecognizer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.CrossSlidingState.Completed
member.summary: The swipe or slide gesture has stopped, the CrossSliding interaction has been completed, and the touch contact lifted.

member.summary: The dragging interaction is in progress.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.DraggingState.Completed

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings
member.summary: Specifies the interactions that are supported by an application.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.None
member.summary: Disable support for gestures and manipulations.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.Tap
member.summary: Enable support for the tap gesture.Touch: tapMouse: left button clickPen/stylus: tap

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.DoubleTap
member.summary: Enable support for the double-tap gesture.Touch: double tapMouse: left button double clickPen/stylus: double tapThis gesture can be used to select a word or open a file or folder.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.Hold
member.summary: Enable support for the press and hold gesture (from a single touch or pen/stylus contact). The Holding event is raised if a time threshold is crossed before the contact is lifted, an additional contact is detected, or a gesture is started.Touch: press and holdPen/stylus: press and holdThis gesture can be used to display a context menu.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.HoldWithMouse
member.summary: Enable support for the press and hold gesture through the left button on a mouse. The Holding event is raised if a time threshold is crossed before the left button is released or a gesture is started.This gesture can be used to display a context menu.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.RightTap
member.summary: Enable support for a right-tap interaction. The RightTapped event is raised when the contact is lifted or the mouse button released.Touch: press and hold Mouse: press and hold, right button clickPen/stylus: press and hold, tap with barrel button pressedThis gesture can be used to display a context menu.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.Drag
member.summary: Enable support for the slide or swipe gesture with a mouse or pen/stylus (single contact). The Dragging event is raised when either gesture is detected.This gesture can be used for text selection, selecting or rearranging objects, or scrolling and panning.Mouse and pen/stylus input does not raise manipulation events (ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted) during the course of this interaction.Specifying support for Drag and one or more of the manipulation settings enables a single device to perform multiple actions. For example, the slide or swipe gesture can be performed with the left mouse button to select text while the wheel button can be rolled to scroll content.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateX
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the horizontal axis. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateY
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the vertical axis. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateRailsX
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the horizontal axis using rails (guides). The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateRailsY
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the vertical axis using rails (guides). The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationRotate
member.summary: Enable support for the rotation gesture through pointer input. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationScale
member.summary: Enable support for the pinch or stretch gesture through pointer input. These gestures can be used for optical or semantic zoom and resizing an object. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateInertia
member.summary: Enable support for translation inertia after the slide gesture (through pointer input) is complete. The ManipulationInertiaStarting event is raised if inertia is enabled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationRotateInertia
member.summary: Enable support for rotation inertia after the rotate gesture (through pointer input) is complete. The ManipulationInertiaStarting event is raised if inertia is enabled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationScaleInertia
member.summary: Enable support for scaling inertia after the pinch or stretch gesture (through pointer input) is complete. The ManipulationInertiaStarting event is raised if inertia is enabled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.CrossSlide
member.summary: Enable support for the CrossSliding interaction when using the slide or swipe gesture through a single touch contact.This gesture can be used for selecting or rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationMultipleFingerPanning
member.summary: Enable panning and disable zoom when two or more touch contacts are detected.Prevents unintentional zoom interactions when panning with multiple fingers.

If the context menu does not fit in the preferred placement, another placement that does not cover the selection is used. If the context menu does not fit anywhere else, a placement that partially or wholly covers the selection is used.

member.summary: None of the following options is used.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.AdjustCrlf
member.summary: If the starting character position is in the middle of a construct such as a CRLF (U+000D U+000A), surrogate pair, variation-selector sequence, or table-row delimiter, move to the beginning of the construct.

member.summary: Use carriage return/line feed (CR/LF) in place of a carriage return.

member.summary: Retrieve text including the alternate text for the images in the range.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.AllowFinalEop
member.summary: Allow retrieving the final end-of-paragraph (EOP) if it's included in the range. This EOP exists in all rich-text controls and cannot be deleted. It does not exist in plain-text controls.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.NoHidden
member.summary: Don't include hidden text.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.IncludeNumbering
member.summary: Include list numbers.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.FormatRtf
member.summary: Retrieve Rich Text Format (RTF) instead of plain text. Rich Text Format (RTF) is a BYTE (8-bit) format, but because ITextRange.GetText returns a string, the Rich Text Format (RTF) is returned as WCHARs (16-bit or UTF-16), not bytes, when you call ITextRange.GetText with the FormatRtf value. When you call ITextRange.SetText with FormatRtf, the method accepts an string containing either bytes or WCHARs, but other Rich Text Format (RTF) readers only understand bytes.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit
member.summary: Specifies the units to use when navigating a text range.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit.Character
member.summary: A single character.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit.Word
member.summary: A span of alphanumeric characters, an end of paragraph, or punctuation that includes any blanks that follow.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit.Sentence
member.summary: A string of text that meets the following criteria:Ends with a period, question mark, or exclamation mark.Is followed by one or more ASCII white space characters (9 through 0xd and 0x20), or the Unicode paragraph separator (0x2029). The trailing white space is part of the sentence.The last sentence in a story does not need to have a period, question mark, or exclamation mark.Other sentences must follow a sentence end and cannot begin with a period, question mark, or exclamation mark. The start of a story qualifies as the start of a Sentence, even if the string there doesn't qualify as a sentence grammatically.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit.Paragraph
member.summary: A string of text terminated by an end-of-paragraph mark, such as carriage return/line feed (CR/LF), carriage return (CR), vertical tab(VT), line feed (LF), form feed (FF), or the Unicode paragraph separator (0x2029).

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit.Line
member.summary: A single line of text on a display, provided that the display is associated with the range. If no display is associated with a range, Line is treated as Paragraph. A selection automatically has a display.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit.Story
member.summary: A story, which is a contiguous range of text in a document. For example, a story can contain one of the various parts of a document, such as the main text of a document, headers and footers, footnotes, or annotations. In a rich edit control, there is only one story per document, although a client can use multiple documents to represent multiple stories.

member.summary: Provides access to an instance of a background task.

member.summary: Attaches a cancellation event handler to the background task instance.
