member.summary: Informs the system that the background task might continue to perform work after the IBackgroundTask.Run method returns.
member.returns: A background task deferral.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.WebUI.WebUIBackgroundTaskInstanceRuntimeClass.InstanceId
member.summary: Gets the instance ID of the background task instance.
member.returns: A unique identifier for the background task instance. This identifier is generated by the system when the instance is created.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.WebUI.WebUIBackgroundTaskInstanceRuntimeClass.Progress
member.summary: Gets or sets progress status for a background task instance.
member.returns: A value defined by the application to indicate the task's progress.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.WebUI.WebUIBackgroundTaskInstanceRuntimeClass.Succeeded
member.summary: Gets or sets the success value for the background task.
member.returns: An app can set this property to false to indicate that the background task has failed. Otherwise this property is always true. Once the background task sets this property and has therefore completed its work, the task must explicitly call the Web Workers close method to terminate itself.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.WebUI.WebUIBackgroundTaskInstanceRuntimeClass.SuspendedCount
member.summary: Gets the number of times resource management policy caused the background task to be suspended.
member.returns: The number of times the background task has been suspended.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.WebUI.WebUIBackgroundTaskInstanceRuntimeClass.Task
member.summary: Gets access to the registered background task for this background task instance.
member.returns: An interface that provides access to the registered background task.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.WebUI.WebUIBackgroundTaskInstanceRuntimeClass.TriggerDetails
member.summary: Gets additional information associated with a background task instance.
member.returns: Represents additional information for the background task. If the background task is triggered by a mobile network operator notification, this property is an instance of a NetworkOperatorNotificationEventDetails class. If the background task is triggered by a system event or time event, this property is not used.

member.summary: Text is not trimmed.

member.summary: Introduced in Windows 8.1. Text is trimmed at a character boundary. An ellipsis (...) is drawn in place of remaining text.

member.summary: Text is trimmed at a word boundary. An ellipsis (...) is drawn in place of remaining text.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextTrimming.Clip
member.summary: Introduced in Windows 8.1. Text is trimmed at a pixel level, visually clipping the excess glyphs.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping
member.summary: Specifies whether text wraps when it reaches the edge of its container.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping.NoWrap
member.summary: No line wrapping is performed.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping.Wrap
member.summary: Line breaking occurs if a line of text overflows beyond the available width of its container. Line breaking occurs even if the text logic can't determine any line break opportunity. For example, if a very long word is constrained in a fixed-width container that can't scroll, it will wrap at a point that might be in the middle of a word.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping.WrapWholeWords
member.summary: Introduced in Windows 8.1. Line-breaking occurs if the line overflows beyond the available block width. A line may overflow beyond the block width if the text logic can't determine a line break opportunity. For example, if a very long word is constrained in a fixed-width container that can't scroll, it will overflow the long word and continue the text after the long word on the next line. Not supported by all controls; see Remarks.

member.summary: Contains values that are used by the IScrollProvider pattern to indicate the direction and distance to scroll.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.LargeDecrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in large decrements, which is equivalent to pressing the PAGE UP key or to clicking a blank part of a scrollbar. If the distance represented by the PAGE UP key is not a relevant amount for the control, or if no scrollbar exists, the value represents an amount equal to the size of the currently visible window.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.SmallDecrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in small decrements, which is equivalent to pressing an arrow key or to clicking the arrow button on a scrollbar.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.NoAmount
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling should not be performed.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.LargeIncrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in large increments, which is equivalent to pressing the PAGE DOWN key or to clicking a blank part of a scrollbar. If the distance represented by the PAGE DOWN key is not a relevant amount for the control, or if no scrollbar exists, the value represents an amount equal to the size of the currently visible region.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.SmallIncrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in small increments, which is equivalent to pressing an arrow key or to clicking the arrow button on a scrollbar.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollBarVisibility.Disabled
member.summary: A ScrollBar does not appear even when the viewport cannot display all of the content. Scrolling is disabled. The dimension of the content is set to the corresponding dimension of the ScrollViewer parent. For a horizontal ScrollBar, the width of the content is set to the ViewportWidth of the ScrollViewer. For a vertical ScrollBar, the height of the content is set to the ViewportHeight of the ScrollViewer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollBarVisibility.Auto
member.summary: A ScrollBar appears only when the viewport cannot display all of the content. The dimension of the content is set to the corresponding dimension of the ScrollViewer parent. For a horizontal ScrollBar, the width of the content is set to the ViewportWidth of the ScrollViewer. For a vertical ScrollBar, the height of the content is set to the ViewportHeight of the ScrollViewer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollBarVisibility.Hidden
member.summary: A ScrollBar does not appear even when the viewport cannot display all of the content. Scrolling is still enabled, and can occur through touch, keyboard, or mouse wheel interaction. The dimension of the content is not affected by the dimension of the ScrollViewer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollBarVisibility.Visible
member.summary: A ScrollBar always appears. The dimension of the content is set to the corresponding dimension of the ScrollViewer parent. For a horizontal ScrollBar, the width of the content is set to the ViewportWidth of the ScrollViewer. For a vertical ScrollBar, the height of the content is set to the ViewportHeight of the ScrollViewer.

member.summary: Specifies how the intersecting areas of PathFigure objects contained in a Geometry are combined to form the area of the Geometry.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.FillRule.EvenOdd
member.summary: Rule that determines whether a point is in the fill region by drawing a ray from that point to infinity in any direction and counting the number of path segments within the given shape that the ray crosses. If this number is odd, the point is inside; if even, the point is outside.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.FillRule.Nonzero
member.summary: Rule that determines whether a point is in the fill region of the path by drawing a ray from that point to infinity in any direction and then examining the places where a segment of the shape crosses the ray. Starting with a count of zero, add one each time a segment crosses the ray from left to right and subtract one each time a path segment crosses the ray from right to left. After counting the crossings, if the result is zero then the point is outside the path. Otherwise, it is inside.

member.summary: Provides base class initialization behavior for Timeline-derived classes.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value that determines whether dependent animations should be permitted to run, throughout the app.
member.returns: true if animations can run in the app for dependent animation cases. Otherwise, false. The default is true.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether the timeline plays in reverse after it completes a forward iteration.
member.returns: true if the timeline plays in reverse at the end of each iteration; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.Animation.Timeline.BeginTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time at which this Timeline should begin.
member.returns: The start time of the time line. The default value is zero. If you are programming using C# or Visual Basic, the parameter type of this parameter is projected as System.TimeSpan? (a nullable System.TimeSpan).

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.Animation.Timeline.Duration
member.summary: Gets or sets the length of time for which this timeline plays, not counting repetitions.
member.returns: The timeline's simple duration: the amount of time this timeline takes to complete a single forward iteration. The default value is a Duration that evaluates as Automatic.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.Animation.Timeline.FillBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies how the animation behaves after it reaches the end of its active period.
member.returns: A value that specifies how the timeline behaves after it reaches the end of its active period but its parent is inside its active or fill period. The default value is HoldEnd.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.Animation.Timeline.RepeatBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets the repeating behavior of this timeline.
member.returns: An iteration Count that specifies the number of times the timeline should play, a TimeSpan value that specifies the total length of this timeline's active period, or the special value Forever, which specifies that the timeline should repeat indefinitely. The default value is a RepeatBehavior with a Count value of 1, which indicates that the timeline plays once.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.Animation.Timeline.SpeedRatio
member.summary: Gets or sets the rate, relative to its parent, at which time progresses for this Timeline.
member.returns: A finite value greater than 0 that specifies the rate at which time progresses for this timeline, relative to the speed of the timeline's parent. If this timeline is a root timeline, specifies the default timeline speed. The value is expressed as a factor where 1 represents normal speed, 2 is double speed, 0.5 is half speed, and so on. The default value is 1.

member.name: T:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode
member.summary: Contains the values of status codes defined for HTTP in the response to an HTTP request.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.None
member.summary: The client request was successful.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Continue
member.summary: The client should continue with its request.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.SwitchingProtocols
member.summary: The HTTP protocol version or protocol is being changed.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Processing
member.summary: The server has received a Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV) request and is processing the request.This status code is an HTTP extension used with WebDAV. It can only be returned if the client HTTP request included the DAV header in the request. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 2518.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Ok
member.summary: The request succeeded and that the requested information is in the response. This is the most common status code to receive.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Created
member.summary: The request resulted in a new resource created before the response was sent.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Accepted
member.summary: The request has been accepted for further processing.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NonAuthoritativeInformation
member.summary: The returned meta-information is from a cached copy instead of the origin server and therefore may be incorrect.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NoContent
member.summary: The request has been successfully processed and that the response is intentionally blank.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.ResetContent
member.summary: The client should reset (not reload) the current resource.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.PartialContent
member.summary: The response is a partial response as requested by a GET request that includes a byte range.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MultiStatus
member.summary: The response provides status for multiple independent operations. Specific error messages appear in the body of the multi- status response. This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). This status code is documented in IETF RFC 4918.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.AlreadyReported
member.summary: Some of the results of the requested operation were already reported.This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). It can only be returned if the client HTTP request included the DAV header in the request. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 5842.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.IMUsed
member.summary: The server has fulfilled a GET request for the resource and the response is the result of one or more actions applied to the current instance. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 3229.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MultipleChoices
member.summary: The requested information has multiple representations. The default action is to treat this status as a redirect and follow the contents of the Location header associated with this response.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MovedPermanently
member.summary: The requested information has been moved to the URI specified in the Location header. The default action when this status is received is to follow the Location header associated with the response.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Found
member.summary: The requested information is located at the URI specified in the Location header. The default action when this status is received is to follow the Location header associated with the response. When the original request method was POST, the redirected request will use the GET method.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.SeeOther
member.summary: Automatically redirects the client to the URI specified in the Location header as the result of a POST. The request to the resource specified by the Location header will be made with the GET method.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NotModified
member.summary: The client's cached copy is up to date. The contents of the resource are not transferred.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.UseProxy
member.summary: The request should use the proxy server at the URI specified in the Location header.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.TemporaryRedirect
member.summary: The request information is located at the URI specified in the Location header. The default action when this status is received is to follow the Location header associated with the response. When the original request method was POST, the redirected request will also use the POST method.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.PermanentRedirect
member.summary: The target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI and any future references to this resource should use one of the returned URIs specified in the Location header. This status code is documented in IETF draft draft-reschke-http-status-308.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.BadRequest
member.summary: The request could not be understood by the server. This status code is sent when no other error is applicable, or if the exact error is unknown or does not have its own error code.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized
member.summary: The requested resource requires authentication. The WWW-Authenticate header contains the details of how to perform the authentication.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.PaymentRequired
member.summary: This code is reserved for future use.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Forbidden
member.summary: The server refuses to fulfill the request.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NotFound
member.summary: The requested resource does not exist on the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MethodNotAllowed
member.summary: The HTTP method in the request is not allowed on the requested resource.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NotAcceptable
member.summary: The client has indicated with Accept headers that it will not accept any of the available representations of the resource.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.ProxyAuthenticationRequired
member.summary: The requested proxy requires authentication. The Proxy-Authenticate header contains the details of how to perform the authentication.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.RequestTimeout
member.summary: The client did not send a request within the time the server was expecting the request.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Conflict
member.summary: The request could not be carried out because of a conflict on the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Gone
member.summary: The requested resource is no longer available.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.LengthRequired
member.summary: The required Content-Length header is missing.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.PreconditionFailed
member.summary: A condition set for this request failed, and the request cannot be carried out. Conditions are set with conditional request headers like If-Match, If-None-Match, or If-Unmodified-Since.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.RequestEntityTooLarge
member.summary: The request is too large for the server to process.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.RequestUriTooLong
member.summary: The URI is too long.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.UnsupportedMediaType
member.summary: The request is an unsupported type.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.RequestedRangeNotSatisfiable
member.summary: The range of data requested from the resource cannot be returned, either because the beginning of the range is before the beginning of the resource, or the end of the range is after the end of the resource.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.ExpectationFailed
member.summary: An expectation given in an Expect header could not be met by the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableEntity
member.summary: The server understands the content type of the request entity and the syntax of the request entity is correct, but the server was unable to process the contained instructions. This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). This status code is documented in IETF RFC 4918.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Locked
member.summary: The source or destination resource of a method is locked. This response should contain an appropriate precondition or post-condition code.This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). This status code is documented in IETF RFC 4918.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.FailedDependency
member.summary: The method could not be performed on the resource because the requested action depended on another action and that action failed.This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). This status code is documented in IETF RFC 4918.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.UpgradeRequired
member.summary: The client should switch to a different protocol such as TLS/1.0.This status code is documented in IETF RFC 2917.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.PreconditionRequired
member.summary: The origin server requires the request to be conditional. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 6585.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.TooManyRequests
member.summary: The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time. The response should include details explaining the condition, and may include a Retry-After header indicating how long to wait before making a new request. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 6585.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError
member.summary: A generic error has occurred on the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NotImplemented
member.summary: The server does not support the requested function.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.BadGateway
member.summary: An intermediate proxy server received a bad response from another proxy or the origin server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable
member.summary: The server is temporarily unavailable, usually due to high load or maintenance.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.GatewayTimeout
member.summary: An intermediate proxy server timed out while waiting for a response from another proxy or the origin server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.HttpVersionNotSupported
member.summary: The requested HTTP version is not supported by the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.VariantAlsoNegotiates
member.summary: The server has an internal configuration error. The chosen variant resource is configured to engage in transparent content negotiation itself, and is therefore not a proper end point in the negotiation process. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 2295.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.InsufficientStorage
member.summary: The method could not be performed on the resource because the server is unable to store the representation needed to successfully complete the request. This condition is considered to be temporary. This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). This status code is documented in IETF RFC 4918.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.LoopDetected
member.summary: The server terminated an operation because it encountered an infinite loop while processing a request. This status indicates that the entire operation failed. This status code is an HTTP extension used with Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV). It can only be returned if the client HTTP request included the DAV header in the request. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 5842.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NotExtended
member.summary: The policy for accessing the resource has not been met in the request.This status code is documented in IETF RFC 2774.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NetworkAuthenticationRequired
member.summary: The server indicates that the client needs to authenticate to gain network access. The response should contain a link to a resource that allows the user to submit credentials. This status code is documented in IETF RFC 6585.
